title: Jeremiah 44
paragraphs: ¹ The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews living in Egypt — at Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and throughout the region of Pathros: ² "This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: You have seen all the disaster I brought on Jerusalem and on all the cities of Judah. Look at them — they are in ruins today, with no one living in them. ³ This happened because of the evil they committed, provoking my anger by going to burn offerings to other gods — gods they did not know, gods that neither you nor your ancestors had known. ⁴ Again and again I sent all my servants the prophets, urging you: 'Do not do this detestable thing that I hate!' ⁵ But they did not listen or turn from their wickedness or stop burning offerings to other gods."

⁶ So my fury and anger were poured out and blazed in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, which became the desolate wasteland they are today. ⁷ Now this is what the LORD, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Why are you doing such great harm to yourselves — cutting off men and women, children and infants from Judah, leaving yourselves without a remnant? ⁸ Why do you keep provoking me with what you have made with your hands, burning offerings to other gods in Egypt where you have come to settle? Are you trying to destroy yourselves and make yourselves an object of cursing and ridicule among all the nations of the earth? ⁹ Have you forgotten the wickedness of your ancestors, the wickedness of the kings of Judah, the wickedness of their wives, your own wickedness, and the wickedness of your wives — committed in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem? ¹⁰ To this day they have not humbled themselves; they have had no fear, nor have they followed my law and statutes that I set before you and your ancestors.

¹¹ Therefore this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am determined to bring disaster on you and to wipe out all of Judah. ¹² I will take the remnant of Judah who have set their minds on going to Egypt to settle there, and they will all perish — they will fall in Egypt. They will die by the sword and famine, from the least to the greatest. They will become an object of cursing, horror, a byword, and a disgrace. ¹³ I will punish those who settle in Egypt just as I punished Jerusalem, with sword, famine, and plague. ¹⁴ None of the remnant of Judah who have gone to settle in Egypt will escape or survive to return to the land of Judah — the land they long to return to and live in — for none will return except a few refugees. ¹⁵ Then all the men who knew that their wives had burned offerings to other gods, and all the women who were standing there — a large assembly — all the people living in Egypt in Pathros answered Jeremiah:

¹⁶ "We will not listen to you or the message you have spoken to us in the name of the LORD. ¹⁷ We will certainly carry out every word we have pledged — we will burn offerings to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just as we used to do, we and our ancestors, our kings and our leaders, in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. Back then we had plenty of food and were well off and suffered no harm. ¹⁸ But since we stopped burning offerings to the queen of heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything and have been dying by sword and famine." ¹⁹ The women added, "When we burned offerings to the queen of heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make cakes impressed with her image and pour out drink offerings to her without our husbands' knowledge?" ²⁰ Then Jeremiah said to all the people — the men, the women, and everyone who had given him that answer:

²¹ "Did the LORD not remember the offerings you and your ancestors, your kings and leaders, and the people of the land burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem? Did these offerings not come to his mind? ²² The LORD could no longer endure your evil deeds and the detestable things you did, so your land became a desolation and an object of horror and a curse — with no one living there, as it is today. ²³ Because you burned offerings and sinned against the LORD, because you did not obey him or follow his law, his statutes, or his decrees — that is why this disaster has come upon you, as you see today." ²⁴ Then Jeremiah said to all the people, including all the women: "Hear the word of the LORD, all Judah who are in Egypt. ²⁵ This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: You and your wives have carried out what you promised when you said, 'We will certainly keep our vows to burn offerings to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her.' Go ahead then — keep your vows and carry them out."

²⁶ But hear the word of the LORD, all you Judeans living in Egypt: 'I swear by my great name,' says the LORD, 'that no one from Judah living anywhere in Egypt will ever again invoke my name or say, "As the Lord GOD lives." ²⁷ I am watching over them, but for harm, not for good. Every Judean in Egypt will die by sword and famine until they are all gone. ²⁸ A small number who escape the sword will return from Egypt to the land of Judah. Then all the remnant of Judah who came to Egypt to settle will know whose word stands — mine or theirs. ²⁹ This will be the sign to you,' declares the LORD, 'that I will punish you in this place, so that you will know that my words of disaster against you will certainly come true: ³⁰ This is what the LORD says — I am going to hand Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt over to his enemies who seek his life, just as I handed Zedekiah king of Judah over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.'
